g.data-info: The tough, outermost protective membrane (meninx) surrounding the spinal cord.
The middle, web-like meninx; the space beneath it holds cerebrospinal fluid that cushions the cord.
Bundles of myelinated nerve fibres (tracts) carrying impulses up and down the spinal cord.
The thin, delicate innermost meninx that clings directly to the surface of the spinal cord.
The butterfly-shaped core made of nerve cell bodies, dendrites and relay neurones.
The rear projections of grey matter where sensory neurones synapse with relay neurones.
The broad front projections of grey matter containing the cell bodies of motor neurones.
A narrow channel in the middle of the grey matter that contains cerebrospinal fluid.
A shallow groove running down the back (dorsal) midline of the spinal cord.
A deep groove running down the front (ventral) midline of the spinal cord.
Carries sensory neurones into the spinal cord from receptors.
A swelling on the dorsal root that contains the cell bodies of sensory neurones.
Carries motor neurones out of the spinal cord to muscles and glands.
A mixed nerve formed where the dorsal and ventral roots join, carrying both sensory and motor neurones.
